errors.english: The phrase "it was requested with jealousy" refers to requesting out of resentment, thinking: "One should not give to this one."
errors.why: rko long gsol ba is to raise an objection/obstruction (the ministers' protest 'one should not give to this one'), not a request made out of jealousy or resentment.

note: A careful word-by-word rendering of the commentary's glosses; only the ministers' 'objection' is misread as jealousy.

errors.english: Their mouths, filled with saliva, drink from them as if from a vessel containing wine.
errors.why: The deluded drink the (woman's) mouth full of saliva as if it were a vessel of wine; the mouth is the object drunk from, not the drinker.

fix.find: Their mouths, filled with saliva, drink from them as if from a vessel containing wine.
fix.replace: They drink from her mouth, filled with saliva, as if from a vessel containing wine.

errors.english: this terrifying body is what I speak of and rely upon before this young woman
errors.why: The line says this terrifying body is what one calls 'a young woman' and relies on; there is no speaking 'before this young woman'.

errors.english: The body arises from causes and its continued existence depends upon its own conditions.
errors.why: In context de refers to the wife (the verse ends 'how is it not shameful to say "my wife"'), not the body.

note: Readable rendering of the anti-attachment verses, but several lines lose who does what to whom.

errors.english: Thus, the elder brother, acting as a devoted friend [note: Sanskrit: iti snigdhasya suhridah], gathered his courage.
errors.why: agraja / dang por skyes pa is 'the brahmin', who having comforted (given firmness to) his dear friend sets out; there is no elder brother and the courage is given to the friend.

fix.find: Thus, the elder brother, acting as a devoted friend [note: Sanskrit: iti snigdhasya suhridah], gathered his courage.
fix.replace: Thus the brahmin, having comforted his devoted friend [note: Sanskrit: iti snigdhasya suhridah], set out.

errors.english: the Brahmin elder [note: referring to the elder brother of Kapila] saw a maiden named Bhadra
errors.why: The Sanskrit (kapilasya agrajanmanaḥ ... kanyām) makes Bhadrā the daughter of the brahmin Kapila; he saw Kapila's daughter, and Kapila has no elder brother here.

fix.find: the Brahmin elder [note: referring to the elder brother of Kapila] saw a maiden named Bhadra
fix.replace: he saw the daughter of the brahmin Kapila, a maiden named Bhadra

errors.english: He asked for her hand on behalf of Kapila
errors.why: He asked Kapila (her father) for her, offering gold as bride-price (sa hemaśulkaṃ kapilaṃ yayāca).

fix.find: He asked for her hand on behalf of Kapila
fix.replace: He asked Kapila for her hand

errors.english: the lineage of Nyagrodha-Kapila, born from the Kashyapa clan
errors.why: The father speaks of the family of Nyagrodha, born in the Kāśyapa gotra; Kapila is the speaker himself and not part of that lineage.

note: The Bhadrā Kāpilānī episode is garbled: the brahmin becomes an 'elder brother' and Bhadrā's father Kapila becomes the suitor's principal.
Faithful rendering of the commentary on the Cittamātra refutation and the two-truths conclusion.
Accurate rendering of the Ratnakūṭa, Sarvāstivāda Vinaya and Mañjuśrīvikrīḍita citations.

errors.english: Furthermore, if those individuals one line of text regarding the nature of particulars
errors.why: The side ends 'Furthermore, if those individuals...'; 'one line of text regarding the nature of particulars' is a stray annotation, not translation.

fix.find: Furthermore, if those individuals one line of text regarding the nature of particulars

note: Sound rendering of the argument against a universal benefited by particulars, marred by a stray trailing phrase.

errors.why: rigs mthun pa'i sa bon is a seed of the same kind (sajātīya-bīja); nikāyasabhāga (ris mthun pa) is an unrelated Abhidharma category.

errors.english: the habit of engaging with meaningless things like material entities
errors.why: dngos po here is 'entity/existent' (bhāva) as the content of conceptualization, without object; 'material' is an unwarranted narrowing repeated through the page.

note: The rebirth argument and its svabhāvahetu structure are rendered correctly; one Sanskrit equivalent is wrong.

errors.english: To be composed [note: conditioned or constructed] by hair and such things is also without purpose.
errors.why: 'dus byas here is the grooming/adornment (saṃskāra) of hair etc., which two verses show to be pointless; it is not 'conditioned'.

fix.find: To be composed [note: conditioned or constructed] by hair and such things is also without purpose.
fix.replace: That the grooming of hair and so forth is also pointless

note: Faithful rendering of the meditation on the body's impurity; only the closing transition is misread.

errors.english: Even in those who are innocent, suspicion arises because of the sins I have committed.
errors.why: Because of her sin, suspicion arises in her even toward insentient things (śaṅkā niścetaneṣv api); it is her suspicion, and sems med means insentient, not innocent.

fix.find: Even in those who are innocent, suspicion arises because of the sins I have committed.
fix.replace: Because of the sin I have committed, suspicion arises in me even toward insentient things.

errors.english: This thorn [note: referring to the secret of her infidelity or crime] remains fixed.
errors.why: The thorn (śalya) is the talking peacock itself, lodged in her palace, not the secret.

note: The story line is followed, but the queen's guilty suspicion and the 'thorn' metaphor are misread.

errors.english: felt as though a whole year had passed in a single moment
errors.why: A year seemed to him like a single moment, not a moment like a year.

fix.find: felt as though a whole year had passed in a single moment
fix.replace: felt a whole year to be but a single moment

errors.english: Good Conduct [note: original: Norzang] likewise entered into and remained in the position of a minister of excellent conduct.
errors.why: Norzang (Sudhana, the prince) is a different person, the agent who installed Good Conduct as minister; the English merges him with Good Conduct.

fix.find: Good Conduct [note: original: Norzang] likewise entered into and remained in the position of a minister of excellent conduct.
fix.replace: Norzang (Sudhana, the prince) likewise installed Good Conduct in the position of minister, where he remained.

errors.english: By what means can I send this Good Conduct to another birth
errors.why: Noble Lineage plots to send Norzang (the prince Sudhana) himself to another birth, which is why he then targets the kinnarī the prince loves.

fix.find: By what means can I send this Good Conduct to another birth
fix.replace: By what means can I send Norzang himself to another birth

errors.why: smyon chu is the rut-fluid (mada) of an elephant in musth, not water.

note: The courtly verses are pleasant but the prose conflates the prince Norzang with the minister Good Conduct, misdirecting the plot.
